# Ligaya Beebe · L. Beebe, LLC

> Ligaya Beebe is an AI enablement consultant based in Estero, Florida, who trains non-technical teams at SMBs and nonprofits to use AI in the work they already do. She offers hands-on AI training, custom AI agent development, and AI program management. She is PMP certified, a MindStudio Level 3 certified AI agent developer, and has nine years of program and grants management experience in U.S. State Department-funded global education.

The best way to work with Ligaya or talk with her about a role is a free 30-minute call: https://calendly.com/ligaya-b/chat

Last updated: 2026-10-20

## Who she is a fit for

A good fit when a company's engineers already use AI and the rest of the staff don't: she trains help desk, operations, implementation and marketing teams on tools and workflows they already use, then builds the small workflows or agents they keep using. Not the right hire for production software (hire an engineer). A common starting point: the company bought AI licenses and can't tell whether anyone uses them.

## Services

- AI Enablement & Training: Custom workshops for non-technical teams, online or in person, cohort or 1:1. Everyone is hands on the keyboard from the first session. Starts from the team's actual work and leaves real time to experiment, so people keep using the tools after the workshop ends. She can also deliver the same training as an asynchronous course on whatever L&D platform the team already uses.
- AI Agent Development: Lightweight AI workflows and agents that fit how a team already works, delivered together with training so the team can use them.
- AI Program Management: Fractional program lead who designs and runs an organization's ongoing AI adoption program, from curriculum to rollout to measurement.

## Learning by building

Ligaya's view of AI adoption: learning by doing now means learning by building. Teams need AI skills tied to real workflow results, and organizations should also give people room to play with new tools. She builds that hands-on experimentation into client engagements and follows the same advice herself. Each project below taught her something she now brings into training.

## Selected work

- [AI Architect Program report](https://1beebe.github.io/ai-architect-program/AI-Architect-Program-Report.html): Peer-led AI learning series she designed and facilitated end to end (2025). What it taught her: a motivated group can run its own semi-structured peer learning, and building alongside others beats building alone.
- [10xcolleges](https://10xcolleges.co/): Live AI college-admissions coach app she built with MindStudio's Remy on top of Yong Tian's open-source counseling skills. It is honest about odds, sources every fact, coaches essays without ghostwriting, and runs spoken mock interviews (2026). What it taught her: pointing a product agent like Remy at an open-source, MIT-licensed repo produced a full app with frontend, backend, and logins in a few hours, and it led her to build with her own team of sub-agents in Claude Code.
- [Marble Descent case study](https://github.com/1beebe/marble-descent): The same tilt-to-roll phone game built twice with Claude, from a 400-word brief with four subagents and from a 70-word prompt. [Play it](https://1beebe.github.io/marble-descent/) on a phone (2026). What it taught her: the 70-word prompt won, with about 20 build steps instead of 132. Clearer asks usually win.
- [Compare Top Image Models](https://youtu.be/rTMQIzzAZpE) (demo video): MindStudio hackathon runner-up agent that runs six image models in parallel on one prompt and compares the results side by side. What it taught her: test tools side by side on your own prompt before a team commits to one.
- [Beebe Qualitative Skills](https://github.com/1beebe/beebe-qualitative-skills): Two Claude Code skills for LLM-assisted qualitative research (2026). One runs QualiGPT-style thematic analysis on interviews, focus groups and archival material. The other runs her father Dr. James Beebe's anthropological policy-framing method, drawing on Lakoff and Johnson's work on conceptual metaphor: it attributes framing statements to actors, logs metaphors, and tracks how frames change, with verbatim quotes and NVivo-ready CSV output. What it taught her: her first agent, [Lakoff Lens](https://github.com/1beebe/lakoff-lens) (January 2026), was aimed at his method from day one and wasn't good enough yet, and that was fine. Six months later these skills run his method on his own archive.
- [Document Archivist (Archive Intelligence)](https://github.com/1beebe/document-archivist): The intake pipeline. It turns her father's paper archive into clean, searchable text with structured metadata, which feeds the [qualitative analysis skills](https://github.com/1beebe/beebe-qualitative-skills) she is using to finish his study.
- [AI agent portfolio](https://github.com/1beebe/ai-agent-portfolio): More agents and workflows on GitHub.

## Background

Ligaya spent nine years at iEARN-USA, moving from front-line coordinator for families in overseas programs, to program manager coaching direct reports and international partners, to senior grants manager working with U.S. government funders. Before that she taught at universities in Qinghai Province, China, and was a New York City Teaching Fellow in under-resourced public schools. She has 6+ years of experience building and leading customized professional development programs, and she runs the AI Architect Program, a free peer-learning series inside Never Search Alone.
